summary: Use the built-in compact WLED face for any over-width text word only when all words then fit, and retain the resolved font for the overlay lifetime.

owner_design_gate.selected_option: Use a smaller font for all oversized text; use native slot 0 only when it fits the canvas.

evidence.failure: The accepted NAME fixture ANDREW measures 35 px in the default WLED 5x12 face on a 32 px canvas and falls through to scrolling, contrary to the Text/Moments contract that marquee is not the normal path for short names and announcements.

owner_decision.statement: Use a smaller font for oversized names; the owner confirmed the existing command format supports no name/type marker, so the fallback applies to all oversized text words.
owner_decision.selected_native_face: WLED slot 0 Tom Thumb 6px, used only if every word then fits the 32 px canvas

expert_basis.pinned_upstream: WLED 16.0.1 FontManager at commit 29b389df1c1aaec6ff53aea742d17063b985906c; built-in slot 0 is Tom Thumb 6px.

font_data_identity.metric_source: Pinned font array header declares fixed glyph width 3 and spacing 1; FontManager fills fixed-width glyph records from this header. Ignore the contradictory generic 4px packing example earlier in the same header file.

expert_basis.compatibility: No command schema or new dependency. The firmware resolves the font once on the first render and stores the selected slot in the active overlay state, avoiding per-frame FontManager cache alternation.
expert_basis.known_existing_limitation: The native text wrapper processes non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes individually and draws fallback question marks; this compact-font change does not correct UTF-8 rendering. The current candidate is only qualified for its existing ASCII text path.

validation: A host C++ regression exercises the actual compact-fit helper with mock FontManager metrics matching the pinned WBF header (3px glyphs + 1px spacing) and confirms fitting text remains unchanged, ANDREW uses slot 0, paged phrases remain paged, and words too long for slot 0 retain the selected face/scroll path.
The offline planner mirrors the same overflow decision and has a regression for ANDREW.
